title: Plan the parcel robot's run, basement included

blocks.text: An office building's parcel robot is moving into a new tower that has two levels of underground parking, floors `-1` and `-2`, with a mail room on each. Before every run, `ParcelRun` groups the parcels by floor, hands the robot's display the parcel ids, and prints one delivery slip per parcel. When a recipient takes a parcel, the robot appends their signature to that parcel's slip.
`byFloor` already does the grouping. Finish the three `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/ParcelRun.java`:

items: `newFloor()`: the function that makes the list for a floor that has no parcel yet;
`displayIds(...)`: the ids, in input order, as a `String[]` (the display's API takes nothing else);
`slips(...)`: one slip per parcel, each starting as `deliver ` followed by the parcel id.

blocks.text: The run must work for every floor of the new tower, and a signature belongs on one slip only. About four lines in total.

cases.says: parcels for floors above ground are grouped by floor, floors ascending, parcels in input order
a run with one parcel gets one slip reading "deliver" and the parcel id
parcels for basement floors, numbered below zero, are grouped like any other floor
the ids for the display come back as an array whose runtime type is String[]
every parcel gets a slip of its own, so appending a signature to one slip changes no other

origin.section: A Constructor Reference Makes a New Object per Call; a Bound Reference Reuses One

concepts: Stream.toArray() returns an Object[] that no cast turns into a String[]; String[]::new gives the stream the element type.

A constructor reference takes the interface's parameters as constructor arguments, so computeIfAbsent(key, ArrayList::new) with Integer keys calls ArrayList(int initialCapacity), and a negative key throws.
A constructor reference runs its constructor on every call, while the receiver of a bound reference such as new StringBuilder()::append is created once and shared by every call.
